title: T1597.001 — Search Closed Sources - Threat Intel Vendors
subtitle: Follow a paid-research operation from subscription to custom report, and watch where the SOC gets its only signals.
aria: Animated diagram of an attacker buying a subscription and custom reports from a threat intel vendor to profile a target company, while the SOC only receives a vendor keyword alert. A written version of every step follows below the diagram.

steps.title: Buy a subscription
steps.caption: Through a front company, the operator subscribes to a commercial threat intel portal. Buyer screening passes; the account is ready.
steps.defender: Vendor contracts can require buyer screening and account-audit exports. Add those clauses at renewal.

steps.title: Search for the target
steps.caption: A search for the company name and domain returns two private reports. Every search is logged - this is the SOC's first echo.
steps.defender: Register your brand and domain as monitored terms. A 24-hour search spike is an early, concrete signal.

steps.caption: A vendor analyst assembles public and licensed data into a clean report. The work itself is legal - the buyer's intent is not.
steps.defender: Public org charts and rosters are the raw material. Publish roles, not full contact chains.

steps.title: The SOC's only echo
steps.caption: One monitored-term alert arrives: brand searches spiked 14× in 24 hours. Read and triaged, it is a real early warning. Ignored, it is the only trace that ever existed.
